questions.question: Find the surface area and volume of a box 5 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm, and explain why the units differ.
questions.expected_answer: Surface area: 2 times the bracket 15 plus 10 plus 6, which is 62 square centimetres. Volume: 5 times 3 times 2, which is 30 cubic centimetres. Surface area measures the flat faces, so it is in square units; volume measures the space inside, so it is in cubic units.

questions.question: A triangular prism has right-angled ends with legs 3 cm and 4 cm and hypotenuse 5 cm, and is 10 cm long. Find its volume and surface area.
questions.expected_answer: Volume: half of 3 times 4 is 6, times 10 is 60 cubic centimetres. Surface area: two triangles of 6 make 12, and the rectangles have total area 3 plus 4 plus 5, which is 12, times 10, which is 120; altogether 132 square centimetres.

questions.question: A tank is 60 cm by 30 cm by 40 cm inside. How many litres does it hold, and why?
questions.expected_answer: Its volume is 72 000 cubic centimetres. Each cubic centimetre holds 1 millilitre, so it holds 72 000 millilitres, which is 72 litres.
